title.en: It might rain; it must be Jack

goal.sl: Poveš, kaj je morda (It might rain), kaj sklepaš, da je gotovo tako ali gotovo ni (It must be Jack, it can't be Sam), in kaj je verjetno (He'll probably come).
goal.de: Du sagst, was vielleicht ist (It might rain), was du sicher schließt (It must be Jack, it can't be Sam) und was wahrscheinlich ist (He'll probably come).
goal.it: Dici ciò che forse è (It might rain), ciò che deduci con sicurezza (It must be Jack, it can't be Sam) e ciò che è probabile (He'll probably come).
goal.en: You can say what is perhaps so (It might rain), what you're sure of when you work it out (It must be Jack, it can't be Sam) and what is likely (He'll probably come).

say.sl: Kar je mogoče: **might**, **may**, **could** + osnovna oblika. **It might rain this afternoon.** (Popoldne bo morda deževalo.) **Jack may be on the fell.** (Jack je morda na hribu.) **She could be at the inn.** (Morda je v gostilni.) Vse tri pomenijo skoraj isto, brez to in brez -s: **He might come.** (Morda pride.)
say.de: Was möglich ist: **might**, **may**, **could** + Grundform. **It might rain this afternoon.** (Heute Nachmittag könnte es regnen.) **Jack may be on the fell.** (Jack ist vielleicht am Berg.) **She could be at the inn.** (Sie könnte im Gasthaus sein.) Alle drei heißen fast dasselbe, ohne to und ohne -s: **He might come.** (Vielleicht kommt er.)
say.it: Ciò che è possibile: **might**, **may**, **could** + la forma base. **It might rain this afternoon.** (Oggi pomeriggio potrebbe piovere.) **Jack may be on the fell.** (Jack forse è sul monte.) **She could be at the inn.** (Potrebbe essere alla locanda.) Le tre vogliono dire quasi lo stesso, senza to e senza -s: **He might come.** (Forse viene.)
say.en: What is possible: **might**, **may**, **could** + the base form. **It might rain this afternoon.** **Jack may be on the fell.** **She could be at the inn.** The three mean nearly the same, with no to and no -s: **He might come.**

examples.en: Jack may be on the fell.
She could be at the inn.

say.sl: Zanikano: **might not**, **may not** (morda ne). **He might not come tonight.** (Morda nocoj ne bo prišel.) **It may not rain.** (Morda ne bo deževalo.) **couldn't** je nekaj drugega: pomeni *nemogoče*: **It couldn't be Jack.** (To ne more biti Jack.)
say.de: Verneint: **might not**, **may not** (vielleicht nicht). **He might not come tonight.** (Vielleicht kommt er heute Abend nicht.) **It may not rain.** (Vielleicht regnet es nicht.) **couldn't** ist etwas anderes, es heißt *unmöglich*: **It couldn't be Jack.** (Das kann nicht Jack sein.)
say.it: Al negativo: **might not**, **may not** (forse no). **He might not come tonight.** (Forse stasera non viene.) **It may not rain.** (Forse non piove.) **couldn't** è un'altra cosa, vuol dire *impossibile*: **It couldn't be Jack.** (Non può essere Jack.)
say.en: With not: **might not**, **may not** (perhaps not). **He might not come tonight.** **It may not rain.** **couldn't** is something else, it means *impossible*: **It couldn't be Jack.**

say.sl: **can** pove, kaj se včasih zgodi: **It can rain here for days.** (Tu lahko dežuje več dni.) Za to, kar se morda zgodi danes, **might**, čeprav slovenščina reče *lahko*: **Look at those clouds. It might rain.** (Poglej tiste oblake, morda bo deževalo.)
say.de: **can** sagt, was manchmal geschieht: **It can rain here for days.** (Hier kann es tagelang regnen.) Für das, was heute vielleicht geschieht, **might**, auch wenn Deutsch *kann* sagt: **Look at those clouds. It might rain.** (Schau die Wolken an, es kann regnen.)
say.it: **can** dice ciò che a volte succede: **It can rain here for days.** (Qui può piovere per giorni.) Per ciò che forse succede oggi, **might**, anche se l'italiano dice *può*: **Look at those clouds. It might rain.** (Guarda quelle nuvole, può piovere.)
say.en: **can** says what sometimes happens: **It can rain here for days.** For what may happen today, **might**: **Look at those clouds. It might rain.**

Look at those clouds. It might rain.

say.sl: Kar sklepaš in je gotovo tako: **must**. **That must be Jack: it's his dog.** (To je gotovo Jack: to je njegov pes.) **You must be tired after that walk.** (Po tej poti si gotovo {m:utrujen|f:utrujena}.) Tu **must** ne pomeni *moraš*. V govoru tudi **has to** in **has got to**: **It has to be Jack.**
say.de: Was du schließt und sicher ist: **must**. **That must be Jack: it's his dog.** (Das muss Jack sein: Das ist sein Hund.) **You must be tired after that walk.** (Nach dem Marsch musst du müde sein.) Hier ist **must** keine Pflicht. Gesprochen auch **has to** und **has got to**: **It has to be Jack.**
say.it: Ciò che deduci ed è sicuro: **must**. **That must be Jack: it's his dog.** (Dev'essere Jack: è il suo cane.) **You must be tired after that walk.** (Dopo quella camminata devi essere stanc{m:o|f:a}.) Qui **must** non è un obbligo. A voce anche **has to** e **has got to**: **It has to be Jack.**
say.en: What you work out and are sure of: **must**. **That must be Jack: it's his dog.** **You must be tired after that walk.** Here **must** isn't a rule. In talk also **has to** and **has got to**: **It has to be Jack.**

say.sl: Kar sklepaš in gotovo ni tako: **can't**, nasprotje od must. **That can't be Jack: he's in Keswick.** (To ne more biti Jack: v Keswicku je.) **He can't be hungry: he's just eaten.** (Ne more biti lačen: pravkar je jedel.) V Ameriki, na Škotskem, Irskem in severu Anglije rečejo tudi **must not**, **mustn't**: *It must not be Jack*. Britanska pisava želi **can't**.
say.de: Was du schließt und sicher nicht ist: **can't**, das Gegenteil von must. **That can't be Jack: he's in Keswick.** (Das kann nicht Jack sein: Er ist in Keswick.) **He can't be hungry: he's just eaten.** (Er kann nicht hungrig sein: Er hat gerade gegessen.) In Amerika, Schottland, Irland und Nordengland sagt man auch **must not**, **mustn't**: *It must not be Jack*. Die britische Schrift will **can't**.
say.it: Ciò che deduci e di sicuro non è: **can't**, il contrario di must. **That can't be Jack: he's in Keswick.** (Non può essere Jack: è a Keswick.) **He can't be hungry: he's just eaten.** (Non può avere fame: ha appena mangiato.) In America, in Scozia, in Irlanda e nel nord dell'Inghilterra si dice anche **must not**, **mustn't**: *It must not be Jack*. Lo scritto britannico vuole **can't**.
say.en: What you work out and are sure isn't so: **can't**, the opposite of must. **That can't be Jack: he's in Keswick.** **He can't be hungry: he's just eaten.** In America, Scotland, Ireland and the North people also say **must not**, **mustn't**: *It must not be Jack*. British writing wants **can't**.

say.sl: Za to, kar se dogaja zdaj: be + -ing. **He must be sleeping.** (Gotovo spi.) **She might be working.** (Morda dela.) In **probably** (verjetno) za will, pred won't: **He'll probably come.** (Verjetno bo prišel.) **He probably won't come.** (Verjetno ne bo prišel.) **perhaps** in **maybe** (morda) stojita spredaj: **Maybe he's ill.** (Morda je bolan.)
say.de: Für das, was gerade geschieht: be + -ing. **He must be sleeping.** (Er schläft sicher.) **She might be working.** (Vielleicht arbeitet sie gerade.) Und **probably** (wahrscheinlich) nach will, vor won't: **He'll probably come.** (Er kommt wahrscheinlich.) **He probably won't come.** (Er kommt wahrscheinlich nicht.) **perhaps** und **maybe** (vielleicht) stehen vorn: **Maybe he's ill.** (Vielleicht ist er krank.)
say.it: Per ciò che succede ora: be + -ing. **He must be sleeping.** (Di sicuro dorme.) **She might be working.** (Forse sta lavorando.) E **probably** (probabilmente) dopo will, prima di won't: **He'll probably come.** (Probabilmente viene.) **He probably won't come.** (Probabilmente non viene.) **perhaps** e **maybe** (forse) vanno all'inizio: **Maybe he's ill.** (Forse è malato.)
say.en: For what is going on now: be + -ing. **He must be sleeping.** **She might be working.** And **probably** after will, before won't: **He'll probably come.** **He probably won't come.** **perhaps** and **maybe** stand first: **Maybe he's ill.**

translation.sl: — Nekdo je pred vrati. Morda je Sam. — Ne more biti Sam: v Carlisle je šel. — Potem je gotovo Jack. Slišim Meg. — Da, in gotovo je premražen in moker. Ves dan dežuje. — Morda bi rad juho, ne vem. — Ga bom {m:vprašal|f:vprašala}. Morda ni lačen.
translation.de: — Da ist jemand an der Tür. Es könnte Sam sein. — Das kann nicht Sam sein: Er ist nach Carlisle gefahren. — Dann muss es Jack sein. Ich höre Meg. — Ja, und er muss durchgefroren und nass sein. Es regnet den ganzen Tag. — Vielleicht will er Suppe, ich weiß nicht. — Ich frage ihn. Vielleicht hat er keinen Hunger.
translation.it: — C'è qualcuno alla porta. Potrebbe essere Sam. — Non può essere Sam: è andato a Carlisle. — Allora dev'essere Jack. Sento Meg. — Sì, e dev'essere infreddolito e bagnato. Piove da tutto il giorno. — Forse vuole della zuppa, non so. — Glielo chiedo. Forse non ha fame.
translation.en: — There's someone at the door. It might be Sam. — It can't be Sam: he's gone to Carlisle. — Then it must be Jack. I can hear Meg. — Yes, and he must be cold and wet. It's been raining all day. — He might want some soup, I don't know. — I'll ask him. He might not be hungry.
